newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada launches new, single food inspection agency.
newsitem.headline: Canada launches new, single food inspection agency.

text.p: Canada opened a new, amalgamated federal food, animal and plant health inspection agency on Tuesday, Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said in a statement Wednesday.

"Food safety and high-quality food remain our number one priorities. An integrated approach at the federal level will improve our overall efficiency and effectiveness and better serve Canadian consumers and industry," Goodale said.
The Canadian Food Inspection Agency consolidates branches of Agriculture Canada, Health Canada and Fisheries and Oceans Canada for the start of the 1997/98 (April/March) fiscal year.
The CFIA was proposed in the government fiscal 1996/97 budget.
